chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Do good with the bereaved ones of others so that good is done to your bereaved ones also.

key_terms.تُحْفَظُوا: You will be preserved/protected; implies receiving reciprocal kindness or comfort.
key_terms.عَقِب: Bereaved family or descendants; specifically refers to those left behind after a death.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of comforting others' bereaved families in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the principle of *mu'awana* (consolation) as a reciprocal spiritual investment, urging believers to comfort the bereaved of others so that their own families may receive similar solace in their time of trial. This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *sadaqah* and social cohesion, where active participation in communal grief serves as a means of preserving dignity and fostering unity within the *Ummah*. It underscores the belief that kindness extended to the grieving is a tangible act of worship that yields divine reward and social stability.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 264. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Do good with the bereaved ones of others so that good is done to your bereaved ones also.
